title: Introduce RAG lint + local-eval CLI quickstart with snippet rules and replay harness
author: Priya Nair
description: This PR adds a compact, developer-oriented quickstart that combines a lightweight RAG authoring linter and a local evaluation/replay CLI to make iterating on prompt snippets, tool calls, and retrieval assertions faster. Motivation: teams repeatedly hit regressions caused by small prompt edits and inconsistent retrieval snippets; existing quickstarts show examples but lack a local feedback loop and automated snippet checks. What this PR contains: a new quickstart folder quickstarts/rag-lint-cli with a README that walks through install and local workflow; a tiny Go-based CLI shim (bin/rag-lint) to run snippet linting rules and replay sessions against a local embedding+index mock or live Redwood dev API; a rules folder with YAML-based lint checks (format, banned prompts, output-structure assertions, token budget hints); an examples/prompts folder with canonical snippets and failing/passing cases; a tests/replay-harness that runs a small scenario and emits a coverage-style report; GitHub Actions workflow quickstarts/rag-lint-cli/ci.yml to run the smoke replay and linter on PRs; docs/reference/rag-authoring.md updated with a short section on lint-guided authoring. Security note: CLI supports opt-in live API mode via environment variable REDWOOD_API_KEY and defaults to an offline mock runner for safe local use. The description includes usage examples and a step-by-step quickstart to run locally; see checklist below. Checklist: - [x] Quickstart scaffold and README - [x] Local CLI with mock runner - [x] YAML rule schema and example rules - [x] Replay harness and CI smoke job - [x] Docs reference section - [x] Unit tests for rule parsing How to try locally: install Go 1.20+, cd quickstarts/rag-lint-cli, make install, run bin/rag-lint lint --rules rules/default.yaml examples/prompts --replay-mode mock. For live evaluation use REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxx bin/rag-lint replay --scenario tests/sample-replay.yaml. Expected outcomes: rule violations printed in machine-friendly JSON and a short human summary; replay harness returns non-zero exit code on regression so CI can block merges. Backwards compatibility: no infra or API breaking changes; quickstart is opt-in. Related Linear: ENG-8123 authoring feedback loop; DOC-451 quickstart docs.
